headline: Schumer and Van Hollen, both legalization supporters, vie to be the next Senate majority leader
summary: Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen are competing to lead Senate Democrats in the new Congress. Both support federal legalization; Schumer has written legalization bills, while Van Hollen has voted for reform.

headline: Senate appropriators keep state medical-cannabis protections and decline to block rescheduling
summary: Senate spending bills would keep protecting state medical cannabis programs from federal interference and ask officials to explain seizures from state-legal businesses. Unlike the House, the Senate panel did not try to block rescheduling.

headline: First phase of the federal hemp ban (synthetic cannabinoids) took effect Nov 12
summary: The first part of the new federal hemp rules, a ban on synthetic cannabinoids in hemp products, started Nov. 12. The hemp industry is pushing Congress to regulate products instead of banning them.

headline: DEA rejected medical-cannabis registrations in at least six states and DC
summary: The DEA sent rejection orders to medical cannabis businesses in at least six states and D.C. that applied for federal registration after marijuana was moved to Schedule III.

headline: GOP picks Thune and Jordan, both reform opponents, as conference leaders
summary: Republicans in Congress chose Rep. Jim Jordan and Sen. John Thune to lead their party in each chamber. Both have long opposed marijuana reform, even as the Trump administration moves to reschedule cannabis.

headline: 16 governors urge Congress to pass SAFE Banking in the lame-duck session
summary: Sixteen Democratic governors, led by Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, asked Congress to pass the SAFE Banking Act before the year ends so cannabis businesses can use regular banks.

headline: Final briefs filed in DEA rescheduling hearing; ALJ recommendation is next
summary: The DEA and opponents of rescheduling filed their last written arguments in the federal hearing on marijuana's legal status. The judge's recommendation comes next.

headline: Sen.-elect Talarico says he'll work with Trump to federally legalize
summary: Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico says he plans to work with President Trump to legalize marijuana at the federal level.

headline: Democrats win the Senate majority in the midterms
summary: Democrats won back control of the U.S. Senate in the Nov. 3, 2026 midterm elections, two years after Republicans took the chamber.

headline: Analysis: voters defended legal cannabis; next fights move to statehouses
summary: For the first time in over a decade, no state voted on legalizing cannabis. The only statewide measures tried to roll back cannabis laws, and voters rejected both by wide margins.

headline: Trump signs H.R. 6500, pushing most hemp-THC restrictions to Dec 11
summary: Congress pushed back part of the new federal hemp rules. The ban on synthetic cannabinoids started Nov. 12, 2026, but the new total-THC limit and per-container cap now start Dec. 11, 2026.

headline: Bipartisan SAFE Banking Act of 2026 introduced in the Senate
summary: Sen. Jeff Merkley and a bipartisan group of senators reintroduced a bill to let state-legal cannabis businesses use banks and other financial services.

headline: DOJ moves FDA-approved and state-licensed medical marijuana to Schedule III
summary: Following a December 2025 executive order from President Trump, the Justice Department and DEA moved FDA-approved and state-licensed medical marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III.

headline: AP calls Alaska Senate race for Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan
summary: The Associated Press called Alaska's Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, the last Senate race of the 2026 midterms to be decided.

headline: Two more medical dispensaries opening, bringing the total to five
summary: Two more medical cannabis dispensaries were set to open in Alabama, bringing the state to five. One is a third Callie's Apothecary store, in Bessemer.

headline: Alabama's first medical cannabis dispensary opens after years of delays
summary: Alabama's first medical cannabis dispensary, Callie's Apothecary in Montgomery, opened in June 2026, five years after the state's medical law passed. The law covers about 15 medical conditions.

headline: Measure to outlaw recreational dispensaries won't be on the ballot
summary: An effort to repeal Arizona's law allowing recreational marijuana dispensaries will not appear on the November 2026 ballot.

headline: DEA says it cannot register California medical dispensaries under state law
summary: The DEA says it cannot register California medical dispensaries, because California lets dispensaries sell without a written medical certification.

headline: Regulators move to readopt emergency rules on license designations
summary: California regulators are moving to readopt emergency rules that let marijuana businesses change their license designations.

headline: Gov. Polis grants more pardons, including marijuana convictions
summary: Colorado Gov. Jared Polis granted more pardons, including to some people with marijuana convictions.

headline: MED adopts final revisions to Colorado Marijuana Rules, effective Nov 1
summary: Colorado's Marijuana Enforcement Division adopted final rule changes that take effect Nov. 1, 2026. They target diversion to unlicensed operators, add product-safety and labeling rules, and raise most fees 2.4%.

headline: 2026 session brings biggest cannabis law changes since legalization
summary: Connecticut's 2026 session brought the biggest changes to its cannabis laws since legalization. Two bills expanded business opportunities and tightened rules on social-equity ownership and control.

headline: Marijuana Commissioner outlines new legislative updates
summary: Delaware's Office of the Marijuana Commissioner summarized new laws from the 2026 session, including statewide standards for how counties can restrict marijuana businesses through zoning and licensing.

headline: Regulators reject 19 social-equity applicants tied to a 'predatory' firm
summary: Delaware regulators rejected at least 19 social-equity license applicants after finding ties to an Arizona consulting firm accused of taking over social-equity programs in other states.

headline: DC among jurisdictions where DEA rejected medical registrations
summary: Washington, D.C. is one of the places where the DEA rejected medical cannabis businesses that applied for federal registration after rescheduling.

headline: OMMU files proposed rules on medical cannabis delivery devices
summary: Florida regulators filed proposed rules on medical cannabis delivery devices.

headline: Regulators propose banning celebrity endorsements in MMJ marketing
summary: Florida's medical marijuana office proposed marketing rules that would ban celebrity endorsements and celebrity-branded medical marijuana products.

headline: Donalds: 'I do not support recreational marijuana'
summary: Most major Florida candidates for governor, including Republican Byron Donalds, say the state should not legalize recreational marijuana. Democrat David Jolly supports it, pointing to the majority vote in 2024.

headline: Kemp signs SB 220, replacing 'low THC oil' with a broader medical program
summary: Gov. Brian Kemp signed SB 220, which renames Georgia's 'low THC oil' program as medical cannabis, allows more product types and raises potency limits starting July 1.

headline: 2026 adult-use push fades in the legislature
summary: Hopes that any state would legalize adult-use cannabis in 2026 faded: Hawaii lawmakers said they lacked the votes, and key Pennsylvania Republicans still opposed it.

headline: Gov.-elect Sand says cannabis should be treated like alcohol
summary: Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand says cannabis should be treated like alcohol and that legalizing it could bring in hundreds of millions of dollars for the state.

headline: Governor signs law doubling licensed medical cannabidiol dispensaries
summary: Iowa's governor signed a law that doubles the number of licensed medical cannabidiol dispensaries in the state.

headline: Voters reject HJR 4, preserving citizen initiatives on cannabis
summary: Idaho voters rejected a proposed constitutional change (HJR 4) that would have limited citizen initiatives on cannabis, so a future medical cannabis ballot measure is still possible.

headline: Regulators pause hemp-restriction enforcement pending litigation
summary: Illinois regulators agreed to pause enforcement of new hemp product restrictions while a lawsuit plays out.

headline: Pritzker, Stratton, Duckworth urge federal hemp ban without delay
summary: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton and Sen. Tammy Duckworth asked Congress to let the federal hemp-THC ban take effect without further delay.

headline: Sen. Bohacek prepares 2027 medical marijuana bill as GOP leaders soften
summary: Indiana Sen. Mike Bohacek, a Republican, plans a 2027 bill to legalize marijuana for medical use only, as top state Republicans show more openness to the idea.

headline: Gov. Braun signals openness to legalization after state-commissioned study
summary: Indiana Gov. Mike Braun signaled he is more open to legalizing marijuana, noting the state is surrounded by states where it is legal in some form.

headline: Gov.-elect Holscher backs legalization; sees rescheduling softening GOP
summary: Kansas Gov.-elect Cindy Holscher supports legalizing marijuana and says federal rescheduling will make it easier to win Republican votes in the state.

headline: Gov. Beshear urges Congress to pass a cannabis banking bill
summary: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear asked Congress to pass a marijuana banking bill, saying it would help public safety, state revenue and the state's medical program.

headline: Medical program passes 30,000 cardholders
summary: Kentucky's medical cannabis program now has more than 30,000 cardholders, and officials say the buildout of licensed businesses is more than halfway done.

headline: Landry signs bill sharply increasing penalties near schools
summary: Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry signed HB 568, which makes using marijuana on or within 2,000 feet of a school or university a felony, effective Aug. 1.

headline: Terminally ill patients may use medical marijuana in hospitals (SB 270)
summary: A new Louisiana law lets patients with terminal and irreversible conditions use medical marijuana in hospitals. The governor let it become law without his signature.

headline: Cannabis Control Commission advances testing-rule changes
summary: The Massachusetts Cannabis Control Commission advanced changes to its marijuana testing rules.

headline: Senate passes bill letting veterans access medical cannabis without a recommendation
summary: The Massachusetts Senate passed a bill to let military veterans get medical cannabis without a doctor's recommendation and to add PTSD, chronic pain and opioid use disorder as qualifying conditions.

headline: Voters reject Question 8 repeal by a landslide
summary: Massachusetts voters defeated Question 8, which sought to repeal parts of the state's adult-use cannabis law, keeping the regulated market voters created in 2016.

headline: Regulators issue guidance on hemp sales in licensed dispensaries
summary: Maryland regulators published guidance on changes to hemp product laws, including sales of hemp products in licensed dispensaries.

headline: MCA builds process to protect out-of-state first responders who use medical cannabis
summary: Maryland's Cannabis Administration is setting up a way for firefighters and paramedics who work in Maryland but live out of state to get the new legal protections for medical cannabis use.

headline: Regulators publish guidance on rescheduling and DEA registration
summary: Maine regulators published guidance about federal marijuana rescheduling and what it means for state businesses.

headline: Troy Jackson, a reform supporter, unseats Sen. Susan Collins
summary: Democrat Troy Jackson, a supporter of cannabis reform, defeated Sen. Susan Collins in Maine as Democrats retook both chambers of Congress.

headline: Regulators announce recall of products linked to digestive distress
summary: Michigan regulators announced a recall of cannabis products that may have caused digestive problems.

headline: E-services for new 24% wholesale tax open Nov 12
summary: Michigan regulators opened online filing for the state's new 24% marijuana wholesale tax starting Nov. 12.

headline: State senator urges Congress not to reverse hemp-THC recriminalization
summary: A Minnesota state senator wrote an opinion piece asking Congress not to reverse the federal ban on intoxicating hemp-THC products.

headline: OCM accepting hemp business applications for the 2027 program
summary: Minnesota regulators are accepting hemp business license applications for the 2027 program.

headline: New state law restricting hemp-THC sales takes effect
summary: A new Missouri law restricting sales of hemp-THC products took effect, with a temporary exception for cannabis-infused drinks.

headline: AG Hanaway sues sellers; federal judge tosses hemp-law challenge
summary: Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway took legal action against businesses accused of selling unlicensed cannabis products, and a federal judge dismissed a challenge to the state's new hemp limits.

headline: Fifth Circuit nominee touts role in overturning MS medical initiative
summary: A nominee to the federal Fifth Circuit appeals court highlighted his role in overturning Mississippi's voter-approved medical cannabis initiative in his Senate questionnaire.

headline: Regulators publish guidance on patient rules
summary: Mississippi regulators published guidance about medical cannabis patient rules.

headline: Regulators send newsletter with program updates
summary: Montana regulators sent out a newsletter with several cannabis program updates.

headline: Cannabis advisory council subcommittee hears Oklahoma enforcement testimony
summary: A public-safety subcommittee of North Carolina's cannabis advisory council heard advice from an Oklahoma official on how to structure and enforce a cannabis market.

headline: Incoming Speaker Reives: decriminalization is 'on top of everybody's minds'
summary: North Carolina House Speaker-elect Robert Reives said decriminalizing marijuana is 'on top of everybody's minds' and that he wants medical cannabis to help veterans.

headline: Commission forwards rule amendments to the AG without changes
summary: Nebraska's Medical Cannabis Commission voted unanimously to send its rule amendments to the attorney general without changes. It will not grant more licenses until it can charge fees for them.

headline: Commission says no timeline set for product testing
summary: Nebraska's Medical Cannabis Commission says it has not set a timeline for lab testing of medical marijuana products, pushing back on reports it could take two years.

headline: Gov. Pillen signs off on permanent medical cannabis regulations
summary: Gov. Jim Pillen approved Nebraska's permanent medical cannabis regulations, a day after Attorney General Mike Hilgers signed off on them.

headline: Legalization push expected after Democrats win legislative majority
summary: After Democrats won both chambers of New Hampshire's legislature, lawmakers are expected to debate marijuana legalization again, with 2027 seen as a key session.

headline: House supermajority, but override needs GOP Senate votes
summary: Democrats now control both chambers in New Hampshire, raising the odds for legalization. Rep. Jared Sullivan is preparing to lead the push.

headline: CRC hosts cannabis session at League of Municipalities conference
summary: New Jersey's Cannabis Regulatory Commission hosted a session on cannabis at the New Jersey League of Municipalities conference.

headline: Gov. Sherrill signs law aligning hemp rules with federal policy
summary: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed a law aligning the state's hemp rules with federal policy.

headline: Regulators withdraw proposed home-psilocybin landlord rule
summary: New Mexico regulators withdrew a proposed rule that would have required renters to get landlord approval before receiving psilocybin therapy at home.

headline: CCB issues licensee update on federal rescheduling
summary: Nevada's Cannabis Compliance Board explained what licensees know and don't know about federal rescheduling. It said many tax and DEA questions are unresolved and it is seeking clarity from federal and state officials.

headline: OCM opens applications for cannabis nursery licenses
summary: New York regulators began accepting applications for cannabis nursery business licenses.

headline: Lawmakers approve bill to curb illicit product flow
summary: New York lawmakers gave final approval to a bill meant to stop illegal products from entering the state's cannabis market.

headline: SB 56 rewrite of voter-approved law takes effect
summary: Ohio's SB 56, which rewrote parts of the voter-approved marijuana law, was signed Dec. 19, 2025 and took effect March 20, 2026.

headline: State Supreme Court strikes down law restricting initiative petitions
summary: The Oklahoma Supreme Court struck down a state law that restricted the ballot petition process, which had made a past legalization effort harder.

headline: Gov. Stitt calls deportation over an expunged marijuana charge 'senseless'
summary: Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt called it senseless that a resident was deported over a marijuana charge that had been expunged under state law.

headline: Stitt calls for a state question to shut down medical marijuana
summary: In his State of the State speech, Gov. Kevin Stitt called Oklahoma's cannabis market a public-safety threat and pushed to put medical marijuana back on the ballot.

headline: Portland mayor files changes to marijuana business rules
summary: Portland, Oregon's mayor filed proposed changes to the city's marijuana business rules.

headline: Regulators update health statements on marijuana use
summary: Oregon regulators published updated health statements about the effects of marijuana use.

headline: Incoming Senate leader: legalization not a 'high priority' for 2027
summary: Pennsylvania's top Senate Democrat said adult-use legalization is not a top priority for 2027, even though Democrats will hold a 26-24 Senate majority.

headline: Senate flip creates pathway for adult-use legalization
summary: With Democrats set to control both chambers of Pennsylvania's legislature in 2027, NORML says lawmakers now have a path to legalize adult-use cannabis.

headline: Regulators file proposed changes to business operating rules
summary: Rhode Island regulators filed proposed changes to the rules marijuana businesses must follow to operate.

headline: Regulators respond to feedback on QA testing program
summary: Rhode Island regulators issued a statement responding to public feedback on the marijuana quality-assurance testing program.

headline: Compassionate Care Act (S. 53) dies at end of session
summary: South Carolina's Compassionate Care Act (S. 53), which would have allowed medical cannabis products, died in committee when the session ended May 14, 2026.

headline: Annie Andrews flips Senate seat
summary: Democrat Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, won South Carolina's U.S. Senate race, defeating the Republican incumbent.

headline: Executive Board approves Medical Marijuana Oversight Committee report
summary: The South Dakota legislature's Executive Board approved a report from the Medical Marijuana Oversight Committee.

headline: Lawmakers reject bills to dismantle voter-approved medical program
summary: South Dakota senators voted down two bills that would have gutted the voter-approved medical cannabis program, which has over 18,000 registered patients.

headline: Medical Cannabis Commission sets Nov 20 meeting
summary: Tennessee's Medical Cannabis Commission scheduled a meeting for Nov. 20.

headline: Lt. Gov.-elect Goodwin makes cannabis regulation a top 2027 priority
summary: Texas Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin said a cannabis regulation bill will be one of her top priorities in the 2027 session.

headline: Lawmakers prefile 2027 bills on legalization and medical access
summary: Texas lawmakers have started prefiling 2027 bills to legalize recreational marijuana, expand medical access and protect workers from THC drug testing.

headline: 15th Court of Appeals cancels arguments in hemp case after bench turnover
summary: A Texas appeals court canceled arguments in a case challenging hemp-THC limits after voters replaced all three of its Republican judges with Democrats.

headline: DPS releases corrected TCUP expansion awards
summary: The Texas Department of Public Safety corrected how it scored applications for new Compassionate Use Program licenses, which changes the results for some businesses.

headline: 2026 laws move medical cannabis oversight to Agriculture Dept.
summary: Under 2026 laws, Utah will move oversight of its medical cannabis program from the Department of Health and Human Services to the Department of Agriculture and Food by Jan. 1, 2027.

headline: Transition commission recommends lower public-use fines, lawmaker-ownership ban
summary: A Virginia legislative commission recommended changes to the state's marijuana law, including lower fines for public use and a ban on lawmakers owning cannabis businesses.

headline: CCA outlines key dates: hemp oversight Aug 2026, retail sales July 1, 2027
summary: Virginia's Cannabis Control Authority took over hemp oversight in August 2026, new hemp rules began Aug. 15, 2026, and retail cannabis sales begin July 1, 2027.

headline: Cannabis event permit applications open Nov 16
summary: Vermont regulators will begin accepting applications for cannabis event permits on Nov. 16.

headline: LCB proposes rules on financial interests and producer co-ops
summary: Washington State regulators proposed rule changes on financial-interest agreements for marijuana businesses and on producer associations and co-ops.

headline: Incoming Senate majority leader: Democrats will 'definitely' legalize
summary: Wisconsin's incoming Senate majority leader said Democrats will 'definitely' legalize marijuana in their first year in charge. The top Republican senator said he is open to talks but wants to see the bill.

headline: Gov.-elect Crowley ties legalization to offsetting Medicaid cuts
summary: Wisconsin Gov.-elect David Crowley wants to legalize marijuana to raise money to offset federal Medicaid cuts, and the incoming Assembly speaker called it a priority.

headline: Ag Commissioner urges Congress to regulate hemp THC, not ban it
summary: West Virginia's agriculture commissioner wrote an opinion piece urging Congress to regulate hemp-THC products instead of banning them.

headline: Sen. Ricketts: Congress should not delay hemp-THC recriminalization again
summary: Sen. Pete Ricketts of Nebraska wrote an opinion piece urging Congress not to delay the federal ban on intoxicating hemp-THC products again.

headline: Sen. Klobuchar pushes a bipartisan fix to keep hemp-THC products legal
summary: Sen. Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota said a federal hemp ban would hurt small businesses and jobs, and is pushing a bipartisan fix to keep hemp-THC products legal.

headline: Rep. Andy Harris presses Congress to close the hemp 'loophole'
summary: Rep. Andy Harris of Maryland is pressing Congress to close the hemp 'loophole,' saying intoxicating THC products are reaching children disguised as candy and snacks.

headline: Rep. Titus: decriminalization at minimum, descheduling at maximum
summary: Rep. Dina Titus said Congress should at least decriminalize marijuana, and ideally remove it from the list of controlled substances.

headline: Incoming Speaker Jeffries, a past legalization co-sponsor, takes the gavel in January
summary: Hakeem Jeffries, expected to be the next House Speaker, once teamed up with Chuck Schumer on a legalization bill. Advocates see the new Democratic majorities as a chance for federal reform.

headline: Reps. Barr and Craig's Lawful Hemp Protection Act would regulate, not ban, hemp THC
summary: Reps. Andy Barr and Angie Craig's Lawful Hemp Protection Act would replace the coming hemp restrictions with federal rules on testing, labeling, age limits and marketing.

headline: Booker, Schumer and Wyden reintroduce the Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act
summary: Sens. Cory Booker, Chuck Schumer and Ron Wyden reintroduced the Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act, which would end federal marijuana prohibition and let states set their own policies.

headline: Senate leader Paxton: no legislative support for a repeal question; 'hard to unring that bell'
summary: Oklahoma Senate leader Lonnie Paxton said there is no legislative support for a ballot question repealing medical marijuana, noting the legislature could change it by statute instead.

headline: Gov.-elect Hinojosa and AG-elect Johnson back regulating hemp THC
summary: A law-firm rundown of the midterms notes that Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa and Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson have backed regulating hemp-THC products rather than banning them.

headline: Ag Commissioner-elect Tucker calls hemp a 'saving grace' for farmers
summary: Texas Agriculture Commissioner-elect Clayton Tucker called hemp a 'saving grace' for the state's farmers.

headline: Advisory council member Oglesby argues for potency-based cannabis taxes
summary: An NC cannabis advisory council member argued that taxing cannabis by THC potency works better than taxing by price.

headline: Gov. Spanberger's retail framework sets July 2027 sales start
summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed a law creating the state's retail cannabis market, with sales starting in July 2027. D.C. and Maryland shops, which rely on Virginia shoppers, face more competition.

headline: Senate Pro Tem Louise Lucas pleads not guilty to federal charges including marijuana counts
summary: Virginia's Senate president pro tempore, Louise Lucas, pleaded not guilty to federal corruption and marijuana-related charges.

headline: AMCC Director McMillan: opening dispensaries 'is not an overnight process'
summary: Alabama's second dispensary opened in Talladega on Aug. 28. Commission Director John McMillan said opening dispensaries is not an overnight process under the state's strict rules.

headline: AMCC Chair Blakemore calls second dispensary opening a milestone
summary: Alabama's second medical cannabis dispensary opened in Talladega. Commission Chair Sam Blakemore called it a milestone for patient access.

headline: Sen. Huffman's SB 56 rewrite of Ohio's marijuana law signed
summary: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine signed SB 56, sponsored by Sen. Steve Huffman. It moves intoxicating hemp sales into licensed dispensaries and adds new penalties under the voter-approved marijuana law.

headline: DEA asks court to reject cannabis businesses' bid to pause its Nov. 29 guidance
summary: In a Nov. 23 D.C. Circuit filing, DEA said the businesses' claims lack merit. It argued its October letter is not a final decision the court can review and that federal law already bars unregistered dealing.

headline: Four Pennsylvania medical cannabis companies file second court challenge to DEA rules
summary: Four vertically integrated companies asked the D.C. Circuit to pause DEA's guidance. They say their growing operations missed the early application window, so as of Nov. 29 they could not supply their own dispensaries.

headline: Sen. Lankford urges colleagues to let the hemp-THC ban take effect Dec. 11
summary: In a letter to other senators, Oklahoma Republican James Lankford said the hemp-THC limits must take effect Dec. 11. He argued that delaying them again would amount to nationwide marijuana legalization.

headline: Sens. Budd and Ricketts say they will oppose funding bills that keep hemp THC legal
summary: After Sens. Sheehy and Klobuchar filed a bill to replace the hemp ban with regulations, Republican Sens. Ted Budd and Pete Ricketts said they would not support a year-end funding package that delays or replaces it.

headline: DoorDash brings hemp sellers to Capitol Hill to lobby against the ban
summary: DoorDash's policy arm flew hemp business owners to Washington the week of Nov. 16. They met with Senate and House offices to ask for hemp regulations instead of the ban set for Dec. 11.

headline: Senate funding draft would keep the rider that blocks D.C. retail marijuana sales
summary: The Senate Appropriations Committee's posted FY2027 draft for D.C. would keep the long-running ban on the city using funds to legalize recreational sales. A transportation committee report tells DOT to keep cannabis drug testing.

headline: USPS says medical marijuana is not mailable but is reviewing the policy
summary: As Georgia companies planned medical cannabis shipments by certified mail, the Postal Service said medical marijuana currently cannot be mailed. It said it is reviewing that position after rescheduling.

headline: Gov.-elect Hinojosa wants Texans to vote on legalization
summary: Gina Hinojosa said voters should decide legalization and pledged to rescind Gov. Abbott's hemp-THC executive order. Texas has no citizen initiative, so a ballot question needs two-thirds of both chambers.

headline: Sen. Tom Davis says health officials are ignoring state law after rescheduling
summary: Davis wrote that the Department of Public Health must reschedule marijuana to match federal action and start a 1980 research program. He asked the attorney general for a formal opinion.

headline: Incoming Wisconsin leaders make legalization a priority; some Republicans open to talks
summary: Incoming Speaker Greta Neubauer said Democrats hope to legalize soon, and incoming Senate Majority Leader Dianne Hesselbein agreed. Incoming Assembly Minority Leader Tyler August suggested starting with medical cannabis.

headline: Virginia commission weighs cannabis tax money for school prevention programs
summary: The joint commission overseeing Virginia's retail launch discussed using future cannabis tax revenue for school screening and counseling. A briefing projected $11.3 million in fiscal 2028.

headline: Missouri surveys would-be cannabis researchers before new license rules take effect
summary: Missouri's Division of Cannabis Regulation is surveying possible research license applicants about their plans and obstacles. The new research license rules take effect November 30.

headline: Indiana's incoming secretary of state backs letting voters decide legalization
summary: Secretary of State-elect Beau Bayh wants a constitutional amendment allowing citizen ballot initiatives, which he said could include legalization. Two legislatures in a row and voters would have to approve it.

headline: Philadelphia City Council urges state lawmakers to legalize
summary: The council passed a resolution by voice vote asking the General Assembly to legalize adult-use cannabis now that Democrats control both chambers. Councilmember Jim Harrity sponsored it.

headline: Federal judge refuses to pause Illinois hemp-THC restrictions
summary: Judge Martha Pacold denied, without prejudice, a hemp trade group's request for a temporary restraining order against the Illinois Hemp Act. The group still seeks a preliminary injunction and is exploring an appeal.

headline: Illinois issues 148 medical licenses to adult-use dispensaries since September
source: Illinois Dept. of Financial and Professional Regulation
summary: Under a new opt-in law, adult-use dispensaries can add a medical license. IDFPR said it issued 148 since Sept. 10, bringing medical dispensaries to 220 as of Nov. 19.

headline: Massachusetts regulators claim oversight of intoxicating hemp products
summary: Commissioners agreed the agency should regulate intoxicating hemp products and unanimously approved a report on the market. Staff are to bring draft regulations to the Dec. 10 meeting.

headline: Georgia proposes changes to medical cannabis patient registry rules
summary: The proposal would add yearly physician certification where applicable, optional electronic cards (if funded) and limits on where and how medical cannabis is used. Written comments are due December 9.

headline: Republican Rep. Brooks Landgraf says he would back legalization with safeguards
summary: At a Texas Tribune rural symposium, the Odessa Republican said he would support marijuana legalization "with the appropriate safeguards in place."

headline: White House asks Congress to protect non-intoxicating full-spectrum CBD in funding talks
summary: A White House list of funding-bill issues, made public Nov. 23, asks Congress to update the hemp definition so non-intoxicating full-spectrum CBD stays available. It does not ask to preserve intoxicating hemp products.
